entry.title: Weaponizing the Exit: Input Privacy Leakage via Exit Routing Manipulation in Multi-Exit Networks
entry.summary:
Multi-exit networks improve inference efficiency by allowing inputs to terminate early at intermediate exits. We identify a privacy vulnerability in cloud deployments of these networks: a malicious Cloud Service Provider (CSP) can infer sensitive properties of individual user inputs solely from inference latency, without accessing inputs, intermediate states, or model outputs. The attack exploits the CSP's control over the model supply chain.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #infosec

entry.title: AgentTriage: Replayable Security Diagnosis Across Heterogeneous Agent Runtimes
entry.summary:
When tool-use agents write files, execute code, or send data, their final responses do not explain the resulting security events, and heterogeneous runtimes expose the relevant evidence through incompatible interfaces. We present AgentTriage, an executable contract for replayable security diagnosis across heterogeneous runtimes. The contract admits conclusions whose claims cite canonical runtime events and requires abstention when mandatory evidence is missing.

Source: arXiv Cryptography & Security (cs.CR) · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #ml-theory #combinatorics

entry.title: On Extending Integral Distinguishers
entry.summary:
Integral cryptanalysis analyzes block ciphers using input structures for which the sum of a chosen function of the output bits becomes key-independent. However, most methods still test one output expression at a time, so they can miss distinguishers that emerge when several outputs are combined, either linearly or nonlinearly. They are also not designed to capture key-dependent integral combinations, which may hold deterministically on part of the key space.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: HAETAE on a Diet: Less Stack, Less Time on Low-End Microcontrollers
entry.summary:
HAETAE has shorter public keys and signatures than ML-DSA, but the signing stack of its reference implementation reaches $158\, \mathrm{KiB}$ on Cortex-M4. The Low-Stack HAETAE implementation presented at CHES'26 brings the signing stack down to $5.7$-$5.9\,\mathrm{KiB}$; yet even HAETAE-2 still needs $8,718\,\mathrm{B}$ in a realistic IoT scenario, where the secret key and the signature buffer share the same SRAM. Gaussian regeneration further increases signing time by up to a factor 2.6 relative to the C reference.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: Rank Ceiling for Twiddle-Perturbation Faults on the Forward NTT. NIST standardised ML-KEM and ML-DSA in 2024 for post-quantum key establishment and digital signatures.
entry.summary:
NIST standardised ML-KEM and ML-DSA in 2024 for post-quantum key establishment and digital signatures. Both compute forward number-theoretic transforms on secret polynomials. Their fixed multipliers, called twiddles, are a documented fault-attack target.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum #formal-proofs
